vocabulary.meaning_en: an unspecified amount: more than one or two, but less than many
vocabulary.meaning_ar: بعض / عدد أو كمية غير محددة
vocabulary.example: Can you give me some money?
I made an unspecified amount of money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: close to the exact number, but not exact
1) an amount of money; 2) the total when you add numbers
vocabulary.example: Two plus two: the sum is four.
He asked a large sum for a bottle of water.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning
vocabulary.meaning_ar: كلمة متشابهة في النطق مختلفة في المعنى

vocabulary.meaning_en: a word before a noun that tells which or how many: a, the, some

vocabulary.example: You will make your money back, and then some.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a little; to a moderate degree
boring or annoying, making you tired
not too much and not too little; medium
vocabulary.example: He has grown a moderate amount.
Your son has grown some since last year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the same in value or rights
vocabulary.example: All students are equal in this class.

fine_lines.title: some vs sum
fine_lines.explanation_ar: تُنطقان بالطريقة نفسها. some = عدد/كمية غير محددة. sum = مبلغ من المال أو مجموع الأرقام.
fine_lines.explanation_en: They sound the same. "Some" = an unspecified amount. "Sum" = an amount of money, or the total of numbers added together.

fine_lines.title: and then some vs somewhat
fine_lines.explanation_ar: and then some = أكثر بكثير (كمية كبيرة). somewhat = قليلًا، إلى حدٍّ ما.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "And then some" = a lot more. "Somewhat" = a little.

examples.sentence: He worked all day, and then some.

fine_lines.title: tired vs tiresome
fine_lines.explanation_ar: tired تصف شعورك (متعب). tiresome تصف الشيء الذي يُتعبك لأنه ممل أو مزعج.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Tired" describes how you feel. "Tiresome" describes a thing that makes you tired because it is boring or annoying.

expressions.phrase: Can you give me some money?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنك أن تعطيني بعض المال؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asking for an amount of money (not exact).
expressions.example: I forgot my wallet. Can you give me some money?

expressions.meaning_en: Some of the people have gone.
expressions.example: The meeting is almost over. Some have left already.
Some may say this is a good idea.

grammar.title: Some = an unspecified amount
grammar.explanation_ar: some تعني كمية أو عددًا غير محدد: أكثر من واحد أو اثنين، وأقل من "كثير".
grammar.explanation_en: "Some" means an amount we don't state exactly: more than one or two, but less than many.
examples: Can you give me some money?

grammar.title: Some as a determiner
grammar.explanation_ar: يأتي some قبل الاسم ليحدد كميته: some chairs, some money.
grammar.explanation_en: "Some" comes before a noun to tell how many or how much: some chairs, some money.

grammar.title: Some as a pronoun
grammar.explanation_ar: يمكن أن يقف some وحده بدل الاسم (بمعنى بعض الناس أو بعض الأشياء): Some have left = بعضهم غادر.
grammar.explanation_en: "Some" can stand alone and replace a noun (some people, some things): "Some have left already."
examples: Some may say this is a good idea.

grammar.title: Some as an adjective
grammar.explanation_ar: some قبل اسم لتعني مجموعة غير محددة من نوع ما: some animals = بعض الحيوانات (مجموعة معينة لم نذكرها).
grammar.explanation_en: "Some" before a noun can mean a certain group that we don't name: "some animals".
examples: All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal.

grammar.title: Some as an adverb (informal)
grammar.explanation_ar: في الكلام غير الرسمي يأتي some بعد الفعل بمعنى "قليلًا / بقدر معتدل": He has grown some.
grammar.explanation_en: In informal speech, "some" after a verb means "a moderate amount": "He has grown some."
examples: He has grown some since last year.

grammar.title: Words made with some
grammar.explanation_ar: somewhat (ظرف) = قليلًا. tiresome (صفة) = مُتعِب ممل. and then some (عبارة) = وأكثر بكثير.
grammar.explanation_en: somewhat (adverb) = a little. tiresome (adjective) = boring/annoying. and then some (phrase) = and a lot more.
examples: You'll get your money back, and then some.

questions.question: In "Some have left already", "some" is a ___.
questions.explanation_ar: تقف وحدها بدل الاسم، فهي ضمير.
questions.explanation_en: It stands alone instead of a noun, so it is a pronoun.

questions.question: In "Please bring some chairs", "some" is a ___.
questions.explanation_ar: تأتي قبل الاسم chairs لتحدد العدد.
questions.explanation_en: It comes before "chairs" and tells how many: a determiner.

questions.question: In "He has grown some since last year", "some" is an ___.
questions.explanation_en: It describes the verb "grown", so it is an adverb.

questions.question: "You will make your money back, and then ___." (= a lot more)
"He asked a large ___ for a bottle of water."
questions.explanation_ar: a large sum = مبلغ كبير من المال.
questions.explanation_en: "A large sum" = a lot of money.

questions.question: "Some" and "sum" are ___.
questions.explanation_en: They sound the same but have different meanings.
